title: Ephemeral metrics and trace guidelines for fallbacks
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a lightweight, operational-first approach for instrumenting ephemeral metrics and trace fingerprints specifically to expose, investigate, and alert on model fallback behavior in the inference stack. It is meant to complement our existing runtime telemetry (SLOs, long-lived metrics) by providing short-lived, request-scoped signals that make root-cause and regression investigations faster without exploding cardinality in long-term storage.

Scope and motivation:
- Problem: fallback flows (model variant fallback, region fallback, capacity-tier fallback, or graceful degrade to smaller models) are frequent and high-impact to latency/cost/quality. These flows are hard to debug because they often stem from transient capacity, routing rules, or cache staleness and leave little signal in standard 1m aggregated metrics.
- Goal: Provide a consistent set of ephemeral counters and trace annotations that are cheap to emit, easy to sample, and designed for short retention analysis and high-fidelity trace reconstruction.

Definitions (explicit):
- Ephemeral metric: a request-scoped counter/gauge, emitted at request completion or at a meaningful state transition, intended for short retention (1–7 days) and aggregation into low-cardinality rollups. Not a replacement for long-term SLI metrics.
- Trace fingerprint: a small set of span attributes + pseudo-hash that can be used to quickly find the representative trace(s) for a behavioral pattern (e.g., fallback-reason=capacity; kv_cache_hit=false; model_variant=redwood-7b-q4).

Canonical ephemeral metrics (name, type, when to emit, note):
- inference.fallback.count (counter) — emit once per request when a fallback occurs. Tag: fallback_reason (capacity|region|qos|quality|kv-miss), fallback_target (variant id), original_model (id).
- inference.kv_cache.hit (counter) — emit on completion: 1 if prefix cache hit, 0 otherwise. Also tag: cache_strategy (local|global|no-cache).
- inference.kv_cache.staleness_ms (gauge) — measured staleness of KV cache entry used; emit when applicable.
- inference.routing.decision (counter) — emits decision path (primary|canary|fallback|manual) for rollout debugging.
- inference.quantize.quality-regression (counter) — lightweight signal when quantized variant triggered quality heuristic fallback.
- inference.fallback.latency-delta_ms (gauge) — time delta between original expected latency and post-fallback latency; helps prioritize regression impact.

Low-cardinality rollups (for dashboards):
- Rollup keys: minute, model_family, region, fallback_reason. Avoid including request_id/session_id in rollups.
- Default aggregation: count, p50/p95 of latency-delta_ms, sum of kv_cache.hit.

Trace fingerprinting and span annotations (recommended keys):
- trace.fingerprint: simple 8-char hex derived from (model_family + fallback_reason + route_version) — stored as span.tag for quick search.
- span.tags to add at root span: fallback=true|false, fallback_reason=(see above), fallback_target, kv_cache_hit=true|false, kv_cache_staleness_ms, routing_path.
- When recording traces for fallbacks, ensure the root span includes the original model id and selected model id. Do not include raw prompt content.

Sampling strategy (cost-aware):
- Always sample 100% of traces where inference.fallback.count > 0 for the first 24 hours after a new rollout or config change (auto-enabled by rollout controller).
- Severity-weighted sampling: if fallback_rate is below 1% global, sample 100% of fallback traces; if between 1–5% sample 50%; above 5% sample 10% but increase sampling for errors/latency anomalies.
- For non-fallback traces: baseline sample 0.5–1% for health; increase to 3% while investigating spike windows.

Dashboard composition notes (layout + widgets):
- Top row: live fallback rate (1m), total requests, fallback_rate_by_model_family (heatmap).
- Middle row: latency-delta p50/p95 for fallback vs baseline; kv_cache_hit ratio trend; region breakdown of fallback_rate.
- Bottom row: recent trace fingerprints (list) with link to example traces; rollout events overlay (clickable).
- Widget behaviors: allow quick filter by fallback_reason, model_family, and timeframe (customizable to 5m/1h/24h).
- Avoid high-cardinality dropdowns by using fingerprint-based grouping; show top-10 fingerprints in the last N minutes.

Investigation playbook (quick):
1) Confirm symptom: dashboard fallback_rate spike -> note timeframe and affected model_family/region/fingerprint.
2) Pull top fingerprints and open representative traces. Check span tags: fallback_reason, kv_cache_hit, routing_path.
3) Correlate with infra signals: node GPU utilization, scheduler throttles, Dedicated capacity alerts (linked via rollout overlay).
4) Check recent config/rollout changes (rollout controller events) — always correlate.
5) If kv_cache_staleness_ms high: consider cache invalidation or TTL tuning; if routing/capacity: consider autoscale or temporary capacity bump.
6) Postmortem: if fallback caused customer-facing regression, generate compact postmortem with: root cause, timeline, mitigation, and metric rollup (fallback_rate, p95 latency-delta, affected requests count).

Privacy and cost constraints:
- Never include request text or user PII as span tags. Use model ids and fingerprint hashes only.
- Ephemeral metrics are short-retention; retain high-cardinality traces for a shorter window (e.g., 7 days) unless escalated.

Implementation notes and action items:
- Engineering tickets: INFR-1234 wires up ephemeral metrics in the serving runtime (emit low-overhead counters at state transitions).
- Observability: add dashboard template and rollup queries (owner: @Diego).
- Release/workflow: instrument auto-enable 24h full sampling for newly created rollouts (coord with release-engineering).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should fingerprint be deterministic across deployments? (Pros: grouping; Cons: leak of config identity). Proposal: include model_family + fallback_reason + quantization_profile but hash with a stable salt per environment.
- Retention policy: 7 days default for ephemeral metrics, 90 days for aggregated rollups. Need infra cost estimates.

Next steps (short):
- Prototype in staging: emit fallback counters + trace tags for 2 canary customers for 2 weeks.
- Validate dashboard noise and sampling rates.
- Iterate on fingerprint schema and finalize retention policy.

Appendix: example metric emit pseudo-lines (runtime):
- emit_counter("inference.fallback.count", tags={"fallback_reason":"capacity","fallback_target":"rw-3b-q4", "original_model":"rw-7b"})
- emit_gauge("inference.kv_cache.staleness_ms", value=235, tags={"model_family":"rw-7b","region":"us-west1"})
- root_span.add_tag("trace.fingerprint","a3f4c2d1")

Notes to reviewers: prioritize low-cost, high-signal instrumentation. Aim to make investigations under 10 minutes for common fallback scenarios.
